```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 18_regression_flat_line
title: What if coffee made no difference?
questions:
  - id: sample_slope
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Suppose coffee had nothing to do with test scores in the population, so
      the population slope is exactly zero. We take a sample of seven students
      and fit the least-squares line. What would its slope be?
    options:
      - text: Exactly zero
      - text: Close to zero, but probably not exactly zero
        correct: true
      - text: There's no way to tell
    explanation: >
      Probably not exactly zero. Just as a sample mean usually misses the
      population mean a little, a sample of seven students will have some
      random ups and downs, and the line will tilt a little to follow them.

  - id: sample_ss_regression
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      So in that sample, what would $SS_{regression}$ be?
    options:
      - text: Exactly zero
      - text: A little above zero
        correct: true
      - text: Below zero
    explanation: >
      A little above zero. A sum of squares can't be negative, and any tilt
      lets the line get a bit closer to some of the scores than the flat line
      at the mean did. So the line will always seem to explain something,
      even when there's nothing to explain. That's why we need something to
      compare it with.
```
